response.rationale: Fibrous dysplasia best fits a long-standing fronto-orbital swelling with an expansile lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof and sphenoid wing, causing proptosis and optic nerve compression. Meningioma would typically be dural-based with hyperostosis rather than lytic; osteoma is sclerotic; NF1 would more likely show sphenoid wing dysplasia or plexiform neurofibroma.

rejected.why: Meningioma is an enhancing dural-based mass and usually causes hyperostosis, not an expansile lytic bony lesion.
Orbital osteoma is typically a sclerotic, well-defined bony lesion, not a lytic expansile process.
NF1 would require additional stigmata or sphenoid wing dysplasia/plexiform neurofibroma; the described lytic bony lesion is not characteristic.
